exposure: lack of sufficient help in the hospital regarding breastfeeding education
absence of lactation consultants in the place of residence
feelings of embarrassment when breastfeeding in a public place
lack of a suitable public location for breastfeeding
outcome: continuation of breastfeeding after returning to work
cohort: The study included 419 mothers aged at least 18 years old, primarily 25-30 years old with higher education, one or two children, and living in large cities, recruited through social media.
finding: Various barriers hinder breastfeeding, including a scarcity of lactation consultants, challenges with breastfeeding when mothers return to work, and public spaces that are not breastfeeding-friendly.
